Rashi on Menachot 6b:11:1.hebrew: ואמר רב עלה - היינו טעמא דפסולה, דכתיב בה "אלעזר" וכתיב בה "חוקה", וחוקה עיכובא:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:11:1.english: And Rav said about it - This is the reason it is invalid: because "Elazar" is written regarding it, and "statute" is written regarding it, and [the term] "statute" [indicates that the details are] indispensable.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:11:2.hebrew: שאני פרה - דטעמא דשחיטה פסולה בזר, לאו דעבודה היא, דהא קדשי בדק הבית, דלא שייכא בהו עבודה. אלא גזירת הכתוב היא דזר פסול בה:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:11:2.english: The red heifer is different - For the reason that slaughter is invalid [when performed] by a non-priest is not because it is a sacrificial rite, since [the heifer] is sanctified for Temple maintenance, to which no sacrificial rite applies. Rather, it is a decree of the verse that a non-priest is disqualified in [its slaughter].

Rashi on Menachot 6b:12:1.hebrew: ולאו כל דכן הוא - בקדשי בדק הבית חשובה עבודה, בקדשי מזבח לא כל שכן? ואפ"ה זר כשר בשחיטת קדשים. אלמא אשכחן הכשר בעבודה, וגבי קמיצה נמי אית ליה תקנתא בחזרה, לבן בתירא. ולמה לי הא דרב:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:12:1.english: But is it not all the more so? - With regard to items sanctified for Temple maintenance, [the rite] is considered a [priestly] service; with regard to items sanctified for the altar, is it not all the more so? And nevertheless, a non-priest is valid for the slaughter of sacrificial animals. Thus, we find that [a non-priest] is valid for [a] service, and with regard to the removal of the handful too, he has a remedy through [the priest's] returning [it], according to Ben Beteira. So why do I need this [statement] of Rav?

Rashi on Menachot 6b:12:2.hebrew: אמר רב שישא - לעולם לאו עבודה היא, והאי דבעיא כהן גבי פרה אדומה — גזירת הכתוב היא. מידי דהוה על [אמראות] נגעים:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:12:2.english: Rav Sheisha said - In truth, [the slaughter of the red heifer] is not a sacrificial rite, and the fact that a priest is required in the case of the red heifer is a decree of the Torah. It is just as it is with the examination of the [shades of] leprous marks.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:13:1.hebrew: ונילף מבמה - כלומר, דרב למה לי? מאי שנא שמאל דמכשיר בן בתירא בחזרה, דאית ליה הכשר ביה"כ? זר נמי אנא ידענא דמכשר נמי בן בתירא, דהא אית ליה הכשר בבמה, קודם שנתקדש אהרן, שהעבודה בבכורות:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:13:1.english: And let us derive from a bamah - That is to say: Why do I need [the statement] of Rav? What is different about [removal of the handful with the] left [hand], that ben Beteira deems it valid on the return, since it had a period of fitness on Yom Kippur? [Regarding] a non-priest too, I would know that ben Beteira also deems it valid, for it had a period of fitness at a bamah [private altar], before Aaron was sanctified, [when] the service was performed by the firstborn.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:14:1.english: And if you say that we do not derive from a private altar - For Aaron had not yet been set apart [for the priesthood] [at the time when private altars were permitted].

Rashi on Menachot 6b:14:2.hebrew: והתניא מנין ליוצא - מאימורי חטאת ועולה שיצאו חוץ לקלעים, שאע"פ שהוא פסול, כדאמרינן בכיצד צולין (פסחים דף פב.) "מהן לא הובא את דמה", אם עלה לא ירד:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:14:2.english: But isn't it taught: From where [is it derived] regarding that which emerged - from the sacrificial parts of a sin-offering or a burnt-offering [that emerged] outside the curtains [of the Temple courtyard], that although it is unfit, as we say in [the chapter] "Keitzad Tzolin" (Pesachim 82a), "[concerning] them, 'its blood was not brought'" — if it ascended [the altar], it shall not descend:

Rashi on Menachot 6b:14:3.hebrew: שהרי יוצא כשר בבמה - שלא היו שם קלעים:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:14:3.english: For an item that emerged is valid on a private altar - Because there were no hangings [enclosing a courtyard] there.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:15:1.hebrew: תנא אזאת תורת העולה סמיך - כדאמר במסכת נדה בפרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מ:), תורה אחת לכל העולין, שאם עלו לא ירדו. והאי דנקט במה, קצת סמכא בעלמא היא, אבל עיקר טעמא מהתם יליף:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:15:1.english: The Tanna relies on "This is the law of the burnt offering" - As [the Gemara] says in Tractate Niddah in the chapter [entitled] Yotzei Dofan (Niddah 40b): "[There is] one law for all that ascend [the altar], that if they ascended, they shall not descend." And that which [the tanna] cited [a private] altar is merely a slight support, but the primary reason he derived from there.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:17:1.hebrew: וקמץ משם - מלא קומצו. רישיה דקרא כתיב (ויקרא ב׳:ב׳) והביאה אל בני אהרן הכהנים וקמץ משם, משמע: ממקום שרגלי הזר עומדים, שם קומץ. והיינו מקום דריסת רגלי ישראל, אחת עשרה אמה, ובמזרח הם. וקמ"ל דלא בעינן קמיצה בצפון כשאר קדשים, אלא כל העזרה כשרה לקומץ:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:17:1.english: And he shall remove from there - [The verse continues: “his handful.”] At the beginning of the verse, it is written (Leviticus 2:2): “And he shall bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests, and he shall remove from there” — which implies: From the place where the feet of the non-priest stand, there [the priest] removes [the handful]. And that is the place of the treading of the feet of Israelites, eleven cubits [wide], and they are in the east; and it teaches us that we do not require the removal of the handful [to be] in the north like other holy offerings, but rather the entire Courtyard is valid for removing the handful.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:19:1.hebrew: סתמא כתיב - וקמץ משם, ממקום שקמץ כבר והחזירו קומצה משום פסלות, (אחד) ואחד פסול שמאל ואחד פסול זרות במשמע:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:19:1.english: It is written in an unspecified manner - [The verse states:] "And he shall remove a handful from there" — from the place where he already removed a handful and returned its handful due to a disqualification (one); both the disqualification of the left [hand] and the disqualification of a non-priest are implied.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:20:1.hebrew: אלא קמ"ל רב דבקומץ ואפילו קידש - קומץ במתן כלי מכשיר בן בתירא, דאי לאו דקידש מיירי רב לא הוה משמע לן מידי:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:20:1.english: Rather, Rav teaches us that in the case of a handful, and even if he sanctified [it] - [Even if he sanctified the] handful by placing [it in a] vessel, Ben Beteira deems [it] fit; for if Rav were not dealing with [a case where] he sanctified [it], he would not have taught us anything.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:20:2.english: In what case is this said - That Ben Beteira validates [the offering] by returning [the handful].

Rashi on Menachot 6b:21:1.english: [To exclude] the first tanna - Who disagrees in the baraita with Rabbi Yosei ben Yasiyyan and Rabbi Yehuda the baker.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:22:1.hebrew: אי קמיצת פסולין עבודה היא - לפסול, אפילו לא נתן קומץ בכלי, לא תתקן בחזרה:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:22:1.english: If taking the handful by unfit [persons] is an act of service - [So as] to disqualify [the offering], even if he did not put the handful into a vessel, it should not be rectified by returning [the handful].

Rashi on Menachot 6b:22:2.hebrew: ואי לאו עבודה היא - דלא חשיב, הואיל ובפסולין נעשית, כי עבד מתן כלי נמי לא חשיב, ואפשר בחזרה:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:22:2.english: And if it is not an [act of] service - That it is not considered [an act of service], since it was performed by disqualified [individuals] — when he performed placement in a vessel, it is also not considered [an act of service], and returning [it] is possible.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:2:1.hebrew: אי הכי - התם במס' זבחים (דף טו:) קתני: כל הזבחים שקיבל דמן זר ואונן פסולין. וכל הני דמתני' ליתני נמי כי מתני': אחד חטאת חלב ואחד כל הזבחים כו':
Rashi on Menachot 6b:2:1.english: If so - In tractate Zevachim (15b) it teaches: "All the offerings whose blood was received by a non-priest or by an acute mourner [are disqualified]." And let it teach all of these [matters] that are in our mishnah in the same way as our mishnah: "Both the sin offering of forbidden fat and all the offerings," etc.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:3:1.hebrew: כולהו משמע - ולא פליג ר"ש:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:3:1.english: All are indicated - and Rabbi Shimon does not disagree.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:4:1.hebrew: אצטריך - אע״ג דבלאו הכי נמי הויא מנחת חוטא בכלל ולא פליג ר״ש, אפילו הכי אצטריך למיתנייה. דמהו דתימא, מדרישא דקתני דשלא לשמה לא עלו לשם חובה — אוקימנא בריש פירקין (מנחות דף ב:) לרבה ולרבא מתני' דלא כר״ש — סיפא נמי דקתני כל המנחות שקמצן זר כו' דלא כר״ש, דמדפליג ברישא פליג נמי בסיפא, ואמר במנחת חוטא דכי היכי דאין קרבנו מהודר, כי קמצי לה פסולין כשרה:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:4:1.english: It was necessary - Even though without this [clause] too the sin-offering meal-offering would be included [in the mishna], and Rabbi Shimon does not disagree [with it], nevertheless it was necessary to teach it. For one might have said: Since in the first clause, which teaches that [offerings brought] not for their own sake do not count for the sake of the obligation — we established at the beginning of the chapter (Menachot 2b), according to Rabba and Rava, that the mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon — the last clause as well, which teaches "all meal-offerings from which a non-priest took the handful," etc., is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon; for since he disagrees in the first clause, he disagrees in the last clause too, and says regarding the sin-offering meal-offering that, just as its offering is not [considered] choice, when disqualified [people] take its handful it is valid.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:4:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - משנה יתירה אחד, והוא מנחת חוטא, דלא אצטריך למתנייה אלא לר"ש, דר"ש נמי מודה בסיפא:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:4:2.english: It teaches us - [There is] one superfluous mishnah, [namely that of] the meal-offering of a sinner, which was needed to be taught only for Rabbi Shimon, [to teach] that Rabbi Shimon also agrees in the latter clause.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:6:1.hebrew: לא יביא מתוך ביתו וימלאנו - סלת לעשרון, דקסברי: קדושת כלי קבעה לשם מנחה, דשוב אין מוסיפין עליה, ומיפסלא בחסרון. כדאמרינן בהאי פירקין (דף ט:): מן המנחה — פרט לשחסרה:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:6:1.english: One does not bring from within his house and refill it - [i.e., fine flour] to [complete] the tenth [of an ephah]. For they hold that the sanctity of the vessel has fixed [the flour] as [designated] for the meal offering, so that one may no longer add to it, and it becomes disqualified through lacking, as we say in this chapter (page 9b): "From the meal offering" — this excludes one that has become lacking.

Rashi on Menachot 6b:6:2.hebrew: יביא מתוך ביתו - דקסבר קמיצה קבעה, והא לא קמץ בהו. וכה"ג פליגי אמוראי לקמן בשמעתין (שם):
Rashi on Menachot 6b:6:2.english: He brings from within his house - For he holds that the removal of the handful establishes [the amount of the meal offering], and here he did not remove a handful from them. And in a similar case, Amoraim disagree later in this discussion (ibid.).

Rashi on Menachot 6b:9:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא שמאל - כלומר, [אמאי] ה"א דבשאר פסולין לא מכשיר לאהדורי אלא בשמאל:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:9:1.english: And what is different about the left [hand] - That is, why would one have thought that [ben Beteira] does not validate returning [to correct the service] in the case of other disqualified [priests], except in the case of the left hand?

Rashi on Menachot 6b:9:2.hebrew: בשחיטה - כדאמרינן לקמן בפ"ג (מנחות דף יט.): "והקריבו בני אהרן את הדם", מקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה, ומכאן לימד על השחיטה שכשרה בזר:
Rashi on Menachot 6b:9:2.english: With regard to slaughter - As we say below in chapter 3 (Menachot 19a): "And the sons of Aaron shall present the blood" — from the receiving [of the blood] onward is the commandment of the priesthood; [this] teaches about slaughter that it is valid when done by a non-priest.

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:11:1.hebrew: שאני פרה דקדשי בדק הבית היא - משמע דליכא מאן דפליג. ובפ"ק דחולין (דף יא.) ובפ"ק דשבועות (דף יא:) פירשתי:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:11:1.english: The red heifer is different, for it is sanctified for Temple maintenance - This implies that no one disagrees [with this]. And in the first chapter of Chullin (11a) and in the first chapter of Shevuot (11b) I explained [this]:

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:14:1.hebrew: וכי תימא מבמה לא ילפינן - פירש בקונטרס: קודם שנבדל אהרן — משמע שרוצה לומר דלאחר אהרן לא הותר זר בבמה. וא"א לומר כן, כדמוכח בפ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיח.), דדריש איש (איש) להכשיר את הזר, והיינו לאחר שנבדל אהרן. ועוד מצינו (שמואל א יג) שאול ושמואל שהקריבו בבמה:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:14:1.english: And if you say that we do not derive [halakhot] from a private altar - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: "Before Aaron was set apart" — this implies that he means that after Aaron, a non-priest was not permitted [to sacrifice] on a private altar. But it is impossible to say so, as is proven in the last chapter of Zevachim (118a), which expounds [the word] "ish" ("any man") as rendering a non-priest fit [to sacrifice on a private altar]; and that refers to the time after Aaron was set apart. Furthermore, we find (I Samuel 13) that Saul and Samuel offered sacrifices on a private altar:

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:14:2.hebrew: שהרי יוצא כשר בבמה - וא"ת: והרי יוצא דדם כשר בבמה, ותנן בפ' המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פד.): "ושיצא דמה חוץ לקלעים, לרבי יהודה אם עלתה תרד"? וי"ל דהאברין ודאי ירדו, אבל הדם אינו מתקנח מכותלי המזבח:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:14:2.english: "For an item that emerged is valid on a private altar" - And if you ask: But the blood that emerged is valid on a private altar, and we learned in the chapter [entitled] Hamizbe'ach Mekadesh (Zevachim 84a): "And [an offering] whose blood emerged beyond the curtains [of the courtyard], according to Rabbi Yehuda, if it ascended [the altar] it shall descend"? And one can answer: The limbs, certainly, shall descend, but the blood cannot be wiped off from the walls of the altar.

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:16:1.hebrew: אלא טעמא דאשמועינן - בשום מקום לא פריך בענין זה, דקשיא ליה הכא: אמאי איצטריך ליה לרב לאשמועינן הא דתניא בברייתא? ושמא שגורה היתה בפי כל:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:16:1.english: Rather, the reason that [Rav] taught us - In no [other] place does [the Gemara] object in this manner, that it is difficult for it here: Why was it necessary for Rav to teach us that which is taught in a baraita? And perhaps [this baraita] was fluent in everyone's mouth.

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:17:1.hebrew: ממקום שרגלי הזר עומדות - לקמן בפירקין מפרש: אצטריך, סד"א הואיל וכתיב והגישה וקמץ, מה הגשה בקרן מערבית דרומית, אף קמיצה כו'. ובקונטרס לא פירש כן:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:17:1.english: From the place where the feet of the non-priest stand - Later in our chapter [8b], [the Gemara] explains: [The verse] was necessary, [for] it might enter your mind to say: Since it is written, "and he shall bring it near" and "and he shall scoop," just as bringing near [hagashah] is at the southwestern corner [of the altar], so too scooping, etc. [must be at the southwestern corner]. And in the Kuntres [Rashi], he did not explain so.

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:19:1.hebrew: וכיון דקרא סתמא כתיב מה לי שמאל כו' - וא"ת: בפרק המזבח מקדש (שם), דתנן שקיבלו פסולין וזרקו את דמן שאם עלה לא ירד, ומוקמינן לה בפסולין דחזו לעבודת צבור, ומרבי לה (הכא) מזאת התורה – ואמאי לא פריך: דכיון דקרא סתמא, מה לי חזו ומה לי לא חזו? ויש לומר: משום דדרשינן "זאת היא העולה" – הרי אלו מיעוטין:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:19:1.english: And since the verse is written in an unspecified manner, what difference is it to me [whether with the] left [hand], etc. - And if you say: In the chapter [entitled] "HaMizbeach Mekadesh" (ibid.), where we learned in a mishna that [if] unfit [priests] received and sprinkled their blood, if it ascended [the altar], it shall not descend, and we establish it [as referring] to unfit [priests] who are fit for communal service, and it is included (here) from "This is the law [of the burnt offering]" — [then] why didn't [the Gemara] object: Since the verse is written in an unspecified manner, what difference is it to me whether they are fit [for communal service] or whether they are not fit? And one can say: Because we expound, "This is the burnt offering" — these are exclusions.

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:1:1.hebrew: שלא יהא חוטא נשכר - תימה: במה נשכר? והלא בין יש עמו נסכים בין אין עמו נסכים, הוי כסלע! ותנן לקמן בפ' בתרא (מנחות דף קז:): הרי עלי שור — יביא הוא ונסכיו במנה; כבש — יביא הוא ונסכיו בסלע. ובחטאת של טומאת מקדש נמי בסלע, אף על פי שאין עמה נסכים. ולאו פירכא הוא:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:1:1.english: "So that a sinner will not profit" - This is puzzling: How does he profit? Whether it comes with libations or without libations, it is [worth] a sela! And we learned below in the last chapter (Menachot 107b): [If one says,] "I take upon myself [to bring] an ox," he brings it together with its libations for a maneh; [if he says,] "a lamb," he brings it together with its libations for a sela. And a sin offering for [one who entered the Temple in a state of] impurity is also [worth] a sela, even though it has no libations with it. And this is not a [valid] refutation:

Tosafot on Menachot 6b:4:1.hebrew: הואיל ואוקמינן רישא דלא כר"ש - תימה: לרב אשי דריש פירקין דאתיא כר"ש, מאי איכא למימר?:
Tosafot on Menachot 6b:4:1.english: "Since we have established the first clause as not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon" - It is astonishing: according to Rav Ashi, [who said] at the beginning of the chapter that [the mishna] accords with Rabbi Shimon, what is there to say?
